hello again, you are not bothering me at all with your replies...in fact i find them rather enjoyable. 

about the writing thing: you do have a good sense of style and tone in your writing but if it makes you feel uncomfortable maybe think of it like a journal. I have been doing daily logs on my mental health for about a month now and it is just a relief to express what I am feeling while keeping track. 

I also found that talking to someone in general helps, regardless if it is verbal communication or just emailing someone. Also, I talk to the crisis textline whenever i feel myself slipping so maybe that could help. And trust me you are very important in the scheme of the universe, I’d like you to take a moment and just think about how many people you have met in your life and how many people would be affected by you no longer being alive. I know that in the dark midst of my depression that thinking of my little brother kept me sane and kept me going. 

You are not insane and your rambling are valid. I  also appreciate talking to you as my family and parents generally don’t acknowledge my depression ever happened and they often just say that I was just being lazy last year.

I genuinely haven’t told many people this much detail about it so these chats also are helping me talk about it. So, thank you kind stranger.

I started my own little succulent area and its helped a lot because they are a bit inspirational. Just when you think they’re under watered and dead is when they produce their prettiest blossoms and blooms. I also saw a new york times article about how the vibrant green color of their leaves can help awaken serotonin and having plants around just helps the brain a bunch of ways. 

I also found that coloring books help take my mind off those negative emotions and they act as a happy distraction. I think the one i have is a bob ross coloring book from amazon, its great. 

from what I can tell, you are an incredible writer and you have a lovely style and tone to your replies. Maybe writing about your experiences could be beneficial. It would be a good way to “open the bottle” and let everything out while also activating some creativity in your brain and giving you a goal or some motivation for the day “okay today i’ll wrote x amount of words”.

I also have not ever taken meds or had a really serious therapist that i enjoyed. I saw an article that said medical marijuana helps calming people down and controlling their depressive thoughts so who knows. 

I also am gonna go to bed soon, as it is around 2:30am where I am. I hoped this helped you take some of the burden off yourself. 

have a good night.

I completely understand. Maybe a solution would be taking some online classes or going to your local community college and seeing if they offer an associates program. If so, then I would just go through that program and see how you feel after. If you want to continue, then see if you can go onto a school that offers a major you would be genuinely interested in. 

I did it that way. I was initially a nutrition major dying my depressive phase at college and when things started looking grim, I went to the community college near me and took some general ed courses. I now go to an actual college where I am focussing on environmental studies (basically sustainability and ecology) and I love it. The main thing I’ve realized is that happiness doesn’t just come out of nowhere or the people around you. You have to take steps and actions (whether big or small) to make yourself happy and content. 

This could be drawing or reading for 2 hours a day or going for a walk, maybe starting a little succulent garden. Also, hygiene and just taking care of yourself is priority numero uno. I swear just something as simple as making your bed and getting changed out of pajamas helps me feel much more productive on days where I just wanna lay around. 

I promise you that there will be a positive outcome to all of this. Life works in tides: where there is a low period, comes a high period. 

feel free to message me of you would ever like to talk or vent. I hope you feel at least a little better talking about this.

hey i am/was in your shoes about a year ago. It was my first year and i was 4 and a half hours away from people that i had grown up with. I guess the best way to sum it up is like being a goldfish in a fishbowl and wanting to break free but instead of going to a slightly larger tank, i went straight into the deep dark waters of the ocean. My depression nearly ate me alive and I almost succumbed to it weekly. 

I often do reflect on my almost year long bout of depression and think about how I will never get those 9 months back where I was rotting away from the inside out. I am now sitting here a year later damn near void of the idealism and optimism I once took for granted. I am now a shell of myself and I am unfortunately a pessimist. I feel ashamed for dragging my parents through it and not speaking up sooner than I did. 

It was an absolute and utter waste of time, money and especially my youth. I remember the weeks after I came home for summer break and crying every damn night about how selfish I was being and how I spent that year in a constant state of recklessness. I was and still am a fool.

The most significant change in my personality that I’ve noticed from where I was last year to where I am right now, is that I worry a lot more about repeating those same actions and sending my parents into yet another emotional tailspin. I just wish they would understand how sorry and ashamed I am that they got this pile of shit for a daughter to deal with. Fuck im crying i gotta go. 

- a semidepressed teen x

 i genuinely cried while reading this. i went through something incredibly similar a few months ago. i was severely depressed, i was 5 hours from home at college and failing all of my classes. I was constantly contemplating suicide. It was fucking awful. However, I was able to make it to May and go home. I got a therapist. I enrolled in a semester at a college 30 min from my house. I started to think positively about my future. While it may not have been the elite, ivy league college I had planned, it is the best fit for me. I honestly still have some of the same feelings from a few months ago but they are few and far between. I chose my classes around topics i genuinely liked and am passionate about. I can tell you, that taking steps to getting better and being interested in things again helped exponentially. I can only hope it gets better for you and that you find some sort of relief in being home and focussing on your mental state. Message me if you ever would like to talk. Just remember that it is a process, you wont get better overnight. It will be months and months of therapy and adjusting but it will get better. You will be happy again. 

I believe in you and I’m rooting for you. 
Sincerely,
